candidates: In Vitest test files, place `vi.mocked(...).mockImplementation(...)` calls inside `beforeEach` blocks rather than inside individual test bodies. Inline mock setup inside test bodies violates Vitest lifecycle conventions and can cause unintended bleed-through between tests; setup/teardown hooks are the correct place to configure mock behavior.

In async timing tests, derive wait/sleep durations from the named constants that control the real behavior (e.g., `DEBOUNCE * 2`) rather than hard-coding an arbitrary millisecond value. Hard-coded magic numbers go stale silently if the underlying constant changes, and obscure which timing relationship the test is asserting on.

In code-generation functions that produce JavaScript/TypeScript source code as a string (e.g., `generateModernIframeScriptCodeFromPreviews`, `generateProjectAnnotationsCodeFromPreviews`), all TypeScript constant references such as `${STORY_HOT_UPDATED}` must appear inside the outer backtick template literal—not inside a regular single- or double-quoted string. A reference written as `'${SOME_CONSTANT}'` in a regular string will be emitted verbatim as the literal text `${SOME_CONSTANT}` in the generated code instead of the constant's runtime value.
